transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
At the Ivy League, Cornell University, students gathered Monday for a protest against the school's response to allegations of sexual assault at a fraternity house.
Athena Holloway is a public policy major and a leader of Cornell's chapter of the NAACP. She was among the speakers.
Our experiences may be different. Our stories may be different. But when injustice touches one part of our community, all of us have a responsibility to respond.
So let's say it one more time. One struggle, one foot.
Students are demanding an outside investigation into the university's response to a classmate's gang rape allegations.
They're also calling for the resignation of Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff.
U.S. military has returned all of its long-range bombers from a British airbase back to the U.S.
NPR's Greg Myry reports on the move a week after British authorities arrested and briefly detained five men with suspected ties to Iran near the base.
The U.S. military says all the bombers at Britain's Fairford Air Base in the southwest part of the country have returned to their home bases.
Vice President J.D. Vance said the move was made out of an abundance of caution.
He also referred to Iranian acts of terrorism against U.S. targets in the past, but did not offer details on any new threats.
The U.S. has used the base to carry out airstrikes in the war against Iran.
Just over a week ago, British police arrested five young men near the base, raising suspicions the facility might be a target.
However, the five have all been released on bail.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump is on his way back to the White House from Nebraska, where he campaigned for Republican Senator Pete Ricketts.
Ricketts is locked in a tight race against independent Dan Osborn.
During the rally, Trump signed an executive order aimed at lowering fuel costs.
Republican super PACs have canceled millions of dollars of planned spending in North Carolina's U.S. Senate race.
Some of the money is being redirected to an unexpectedly competitive race in Kansas, as NPR's Stephen Fowler reports.
According to ad tracking firm Ad Impact, more than $16 million in future reservations for North Carolina's Senate race have been canceled since Friday.
Polls show the Democratic candidate Roy Cooper was a sizable lead there over the Republican Michael Watley.
Some of that money has been redirected to the Senate race in Kansas.
It's one of many Midwestern states where rising fuel costs and Trump administration policies like tariffs have hit hardest,
and where enough voters say they've soured on Republicans to make these reliably read states competitive.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Now to Canada, where a separatist party won Quebec's election on Monday.
Voters in the province returned the party Québécois to power.
The PQ won the most seats in the provincial legislature, but it's not yet clear if the party would reach the 64 seats needed to form a majority government.
The party has promised another referendum on independence from Canada.
However, the party leader has pledged to wait until President Trump is no longer in office.
The country's largest ferry system almost completely shut down Monday due to a labor dispute.
Writers hope Washington state ferries will resume service Tuesday.
Casey Martin from member station KUOW reports from Seattle.
Washington state ferries says nearly two dozen engine room workers called out sick and backup crews refused to fill in.
That left 13 of the 18 available boats stuck at the dock.
This is by far the worst day ever that I have seen in the 30 years of commuting.
Christine Virgillo is one of the tens of thousands of people who rely on the ferries to get to work.
Whatever is going on with the state ferries, whatever it may be, they need to not interfere with us as commuters.
It's just not fair. The union representing the ferry workers said the engine rooms are underpaid and understaffed.
Washington's governor said after meeting with ferry leadership, he expected all boats to sail again Tuesday.
For NPR News, I'm Casey Martin in Seattle.

topics.text: Cornell University students protest school's response to sexual assault allegations at fraternity house
U.S. military returns long-range bombers from British Fairford Air Base to U.S. home bases
President Trump campaigns for Republican Senator Pete Ricketts in Nebraska, signs fuel cost executive order
Republican super PACs cancel millions in North Carolina Senate race spending, redirect to Kansas
Québécois party wins Quebec provincial election, promises independence referendum after Trump leaves office
Washington state ferry system shuts down due to labor dispute over engine room worker pay
